outcomes: A service loads its signing keyring after restart instead of silently minting a new key
A rotation installs one active successor while preserving the retiring predecessor during the overlap window
A failed or conflicting rotation leaves the durable keyring unchanged
Private signing material stays confined to the owner document and storage boundary
nonGoals: Choosing an organization's key age or rotation schedule
Providing database-column encryption or a key management service
Publishing revoked or expired keys in a verifier JWKS

requirements.text: The database store persists the private keyring owner document, loads only active and retiring keys, and treats lifecycle and retirement columns as authoritative across restarts.
Retiring the active predecessor, inserting the active successor, and stamping retirement time commit in one transaction; every non-applied outcome rolls back all writes.
The scheduler invokes only a caller-supplied policy, never overlaps invocations, reports policy errors without stopping future ticks, and cannot fire after its idempotent stop returns.

The store's own errors and logs never contain private key material: a failure that has a key in hand reports the key's identity (kid), never its private parameters. The public JWKS projection and signing evidence are owned by go/authentication-authorization's secret-non-disclosure.
